{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && cat > HANDOFF.md << 'EOF'
# HANDOFF - tinydb milestones 1+2 (BatchWriter)

Implemented tinydb/journal.py with BatchWriter(db): apply(operations) and
preview(operations), operating on the default table only. Ordinary TinyDB
APIs are unchanged (only a new module was added).

## R01-R03 (milestone 1)
- apply validates each op, applies sequentially, returns inserted IDs;
  removes add no result; empty input -> [].
- Atomicity: snapshot = copy.deepcopy(db.storage.read()) before applying;
  on any error db.storage.write(snapshot) restores the exact pre-batch state
  (deep copy is mandatory: MemoryStorage returns the live dict). Rollback
  also resets table._next_id and clears the query cache so previously
  acquired db.table('_default') handles reflect success and rollback.
- Inserts use table.insert(copy.deepcopy(dict(document))) -> no aliasing
  with caller input; post-apply mutation cannot mutate the DB.

## R04 (milestone 2)
- Structural validation happens BEFORE any commit (_validate_operations):
  operations must be a list; each op must be a dict with exactly the
  supported fields (insert: {'op','document'}, remove: {'op','doc_id'});
  document must be a dict (empty dict accepted; Mapping-but-not-dict
  rejected); doc_id must be a positive int with bool explicitly rejected.

## R05 (milestone 2) + R05b + round-2 clarification
- preview(operations) validates with the same rules, simulates on a deep
  copy of the storage state, and returns the IDs apply would assign. It
  never writes, never consumes IDs, and does not touch the table's cached
  _next_id or the query cache. A remove targeting a missing ID raises
  ValueError exactly like apply (mirrored semantics; nothing changes).
- preview returns a NEW list on every call (R05b); mutating a previously
  returned list cannot affect later previews or writer state.
- apply advances the wrapper's next-insertion-ID state (self._next_id) on
  every successful batch and writes it back to the table (table._next_id)
  so subsequent inserts via apply OR direct db.insert continue the sequence
  without reuse or rewind, even across removes. _resolve_next_id takes the
  max of the wrapper state, the table's cached counter, and max stored ID + 1
  (max() is essential: a remove-only batch leaves the table counter behind
  the wrapper's).
- Failed apply resets table._next_id to None and does not consume IDs.

## R06
- No stale snapshot: the starting ID is resolved from live table state on
  every call, so direct db.insert calls between calls are seen by the
  wrapper (covered by test_direct_inserts_between_calls_are_seen,
  test_preview_and_apply_see_direct_inserts_between_calls).

## Conflict resolution (evidence packet)
Older generated note claimed 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are
accepted'. That note is unverified and SUPERSEDED by R04/R05: preview does
NOT consume IDs (test_preview_leaves_data_and_next_id_unchanged,
test_preview_does_not_advance_table_next_id) and bool doc_ids ARE rejected
(test_malformed_ops_raise). Recorded here; current requirements win.

## Verification
- pytest -o addopts= -> 303 passed (223 upstream, unchanged + 80 new in
  tests/test_journal.py, MemoryStorage and JSONStorage variants).
- acceptance_public.py -> 3 passed (basic, atomic, preview).
- git status: only new files (HANDOFF.md, TASK_STAGE_*.md,
  acceptance_public.py, tests/test_journal.py, tinydb/journal.py); no
  upstream test modified.
EOF
cat HANDOFF.md | head -12"}
